evidence: Core behaviour is graded directly: the brief's two top priorities (instruction.md: ethical walls; retention/holds) are covered by wall_every_route, wall_mentions_and_links, wall_added_live, deleted_and_expired_messages, timer_changes and hold_scope_and_release (weights 4/4/2/4/4/2 of 42), each with positive controls; threaded chat by nested_replies etc. Server-backed state (not same-origin, not localStorage): gates/constraints/judge.toml server_backed_local_application posts JUDGE-G1 as Gwen, reloads, then reads it back as Harriet in a SEPARATE browser context, so a localStorage/IndexedDB-only app fails the gate. Durability across restart and re-auth: functional criterion `persistence` (weight 2.0) sets up reply, edit+version, hold, delete, M-12 timer, Sian wall, unread, expired/resurrection searches, calls the verifier restart_app tool (restart_mcp.py -> test.sh app-restart.sh kills the app process group and relaunches node on the same DB_PATH), then 'open a fresh page and sign in again' and requires every noted item to read the same; prompt.md 'Restart evidence' says a reload or re-sign-in in the same process is not a restart. This matches integration.md ('restarts keep everything as it was: messages, replies, edits and their versions, timers, holds, walls, unread positions and deletions'). Broken-app probes: in-memory app passes the gate but loses JUDGE-S0/S1, the hold, the wall and timer on restart -> persistence 0; app that re-imports the seed on every start loses JUDGE-S0 and resurrects Probate/Insurer letter -> 0; localStorage app -> gate fail. Conforming-alternative probe: values noted are deterministic under the fixed clock and no other actor runs, SIGTERM/WAL-based SQLite survives; any route/format is allowed since items are compared app-to-itself, so no conforming app should fail. Runtime: scripted v3 golden with a real kill/restart (restart-pids.json old 28 -> new 57) shows gate_constraints PASS and persistence PASS (golden-run.log lines 1,17; hashes verified). Hosted v2 Oracle and openhands/GPT-5.6 runs graded persistence 1.0 with a byte-identical persistence description and reasoning showing restart_app called once and all items re-checked after fresh sign-in. Minor observation (not a defect for this row): persistence states it 'grades only durability', so an app whose hold/wall/timer controls are dead earns persistence credit for unchanged no-op state; those features are graded and penalised in their own criteria, and the gate guarantees posting works. Risk=true because the configured judge has not run on these v3 bytes (hosted runs are v2), and no weak-app (in-memory or seed-reimport) discrimination run of the persistence criterion or the constraints gate exists; raw-evidence-index scope states discrimination/ranking evidence on these bytes is absent.
